page: Amazon Web Services g6.12xlarge is a GPU-accelerated server instance featuring four NVIDIA L4 GPUs based on the Ada Lovelace architecture, providing a total of 89 GB of VRAM. The instance is powered by an AMD EPYC 7R13 processor with 48 dedicated vCPUs and 24 physical cores running at 3.4 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. It is equipped with 192.0 GB of DDR4 memory operating at 3 GHz, 3760 GB of local NVMe SSD storage, and a baseline network bandwidth of 40 Gbps, all managed via the AWS Nitro hypervisor.

Performance benchmarks indicate strong capabilities across multiple domains. The CPU delivers strong multi-core and single-core performance in stress-ng tests, placing in the top 25% of tested hardware. In graphics and media workloads, Geekbench ray tracing and image processing benchmarks also rank in the top 25%. Most notably, the server achieves top-tier performance in the top 10% for large language model inference tasks, including prompt processing and text generation for small and medium models, while maintaining strong performance for large model text generation. Memory bandwidth and standard database operations perform within the average range.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the g6.12xlarge offers a dense allocation of four mid-range NVIDIA L4 GPUs alongside substantial local NVMe storage, making it a highly resource-dense option for parallelized workloads without the premium cost of high-end enterprise GPUs. This hardware profile is optimal for workloads such as LLM inference, real-time ray tracing, video transcoding, image processing, and high-throughput machine learning deployments.
